title: Relationship with Literary Realism
use_cases: Use when defining the historical origins of realistic fiction
Implement when comparing the differences between fantastic and credible storytelling
Configure when categorizing literature based on social context and object detail
Use when analyzing the influence of nineteenth-century realism on modern fiction
content:
Realistic fiction shares much with the older tradition of literary realism. Literary realism emerged in the nineteenth century with the aim of depicting everyday life truthfully and without embellishment.

Realistic fiction can be considered one of the modern outlets of realism in literature: it carries the intention of mirroring life, of representing people in recognizable circumstances. Realism in fiction often emphasizes detail, social class, and implications of setting. For instance, the French novelist Honoré de Balzac earned recognition for his attention to object detail and social context as a realism pioneer.

The labels “realism in fiction” and “realism in literature” highlight the philosophical and aesthetic commitments of authors to depict the plausible rather than the fantastic. The question “What is realistic fiction genre?” is addressed, therefore, by locating it within the broader realist intention: stories that do not pretend to paint the extraordinary but rather offer the credible.
